Cut a split parent's catchment among its fragments by nearest reach

Source: R/reconcile_divides.R
dot-cut_parent_by_nearest_line.Rd

The partition of a split reference catchment among the fragments of the reach is a nearest-channel assignment: land drains to the piece of channel closest to it. The D8 trace computes that by following flow directions, which needs the vector reach and the flow grid to agree on where the channel is. Where they do not, Alaska routes TDX-Hydro reaches over HydroSHEDS grids, the trace lands elsewhere and returns sub-polygons displaced from the fragment they were assigned to, or none at all.

This computes the same assignment geometrically. Each fragment's line is sampled at step metres, the samples generate a nearest-point tessellation, cells are dissolved by the fragment that generated them, and the result is clipped to the parent. Three properties hold by construction rather than by repair: the pieces tile the parent exactly, so area is conserved; no two fragments can claim the same ground; and every fragment whose line meets the parent receives a share, so none is left without a catchment.

This is a partition of one real catchment among its own children, clipped to that catchment. It creates no land and fills no gap between divides.

Usage

.cut_parent_by_nearest_line(parent, lines, crs, step = 25)

Arguments

parent

sfg, the parent catchment to divide.

lines

List of sfc or NULL, each fragment's member flowlines.

crs

CRS shared by parent and lines.

step

Spacing in CRS units at which each line is sampled. 25 m sits below the 30 m DEM cell, so the cut resolves detail the grid cannot.

Value

A list of sfg the same length as lines, or NULL if the cut cannot be computed and the caller should leave the group alone.
